quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I will submit the report by Monday.'
options: She promised she would submit the report by Monday.
She promised she will submit the report by Monday.
She promised that the report would be submitted by Monday.
quests.correctAnswer: She promised she would submit the report by Monday.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I will submit the report by Monday.'
quests.hint: 'Will' shifts to 'would'. The reporting verb 'said' can become 'promised' for a future commitment.
quests.explanation: 'Will' → 'would'. 'Said' can be replaced with 'promised' here because the statement is a future commitment.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The manager asked, 'Were you at the morning briefing?'
options: The manager asked if I had been at the morning briefing.
The manager asked if I was at the morning briefing.
The manager asked was I at the morning briefing.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager asked if I had been at the morning briefing.
quests.sentence: The manager asked, 'Were you at the morning briefing?'
quests.hint: 'Were' shifts to 'had been'. Use 'if' and statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Were' (past simple) shifts to 'had been' (past perfect). Use 'if' for yes/no questions.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The director said, 'Update the client on the project status.'
options: The director told me to update the client on the project status.
The director said to update the client on the project status.
The director told me updating the client on the project status.
quests.correctAnswer: The director told me to update the client on the project status.
quests.sentence: The director said, 'Update the client on the project status.'
quests.explanation: 'Update' is an imperative → 'told me to update the client on the project status'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I can't complete this task alone.'
options: He admitted he couldn't complete the task alone.
He admitted he can't complete the task alone.
He admitted that he couldn't have completed the task alone.
quests.correctAnswer: He admitted he couldn't complete the task alone.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I can't complete this task alone.'
quests.hint: 'Can't' → 'couldn't'. The reporting verb 'admitted' suits a confession of difficulty.
quests.explanation: 'Can't' shifts to 'couldn't'. 'Said' can become 'admitted' when reporting a confession. 'This task' → 'the task'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Which option should we choose?'
options: She asked which option they should choose.
She asked which option should they choose.
She asked which option we should choose.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked which option they should choose.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Which option should we choose?'
quests.explanation: 'Should' does not change. Use statement word order. 'We' shifts to 'they'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'Please don't make so much noise.'
options: He asked us not to make so much noise.
He asked us to not making so much noise.
He said please don't make so much noise.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked us not to make so much noise.
quests.sentence: He said, 'Please don't make so much noise.'
quests.hint: Polite negative request: 'asked + object + not to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: 'Please don't make' is a polite negative request → 'asked us not to make so much noise'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They said, 'We have been working on this for months.'
options: They said they had been working on it for months.
They said they have been working on it for months.
They said they had worked on it for months.
quests.correctAnswer: They said they had been working on it for months.
quests.sentence: They said, 'We have been working on this for months.'
quests.hint: Present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous. 'This' → 'it'.
quests.explanation: 'Have been working' shifts to 'had been working'. 'This' → 'it'. The continuous aspect is preserved.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The manager asked, 'Who is responsible for quality control?'
options: The manager asked who was responsible for quality control.
The manager asked who is responsible for quality control.
The manager asked who was responsible of quality control.
quests.correctAnswer: The manager asked who was responsible for quality control.
quests.sentence: The manager asked, 'Who is responsible for quality control?'
quests.hint: Wh-question: 'is' → 'was', statement order. Note the correct preposition 'for'.
quests.explanation: 'Is' shifts to 'was'. Use statement word order. The preposition 'for' (responsible for) must be retained.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The manager said, 'Forward all enquiries to the help desk.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They said, 'We signed the contract this morning.'

They confirmed they had signed the contract this morning.

quests.sentence: They said, 'We signed the contract this morning.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Can we reschedule the meeting?'
options: She asked if they could reschedule the meeting.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Legal said, 'Keep all records for a minimum of five years.'

Legal said keep all records for a minimum of five years.
Legal told us keeping all records for a minimum of five years.
quests.correctAnswer: Legal required us to keep all records for a minimum of five years.
quests.sentence: Legal said, 'Keep all records for a minimum of five years.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'required + us + to + keep'. Use 'required' for formal policy instructions.
quests.explanation: 'Keep' is an imperative → 'required us to keep'. The verb 'required' signals a formal policy mandate.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'The new product exceeded our expectations.'

quests.sentence: She said, 'The new product exceeded our expectations.'
quests.explanation: 'Exceeded' (past simple) shifts to 'had exceeded' (past perfect). 'Our' shifts to 'their'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The client asked, 'Why was there a delay in delivery?'
options: The client asked why there had been a delay in delivery.
The client asked why was there a delay in delivery.
The client asked why there was a delay in delivery.
quests.correctAnswer: The client asked why there had been a delay in delivery.
quests.sentence: The client asked, 'Why was there a delay in delivery?'
quests.explanation: Past simple 'was' shifts to past perfect 'had been'. Use statement word order (not question order).

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The supervisor said, 'Report any safety hazards immediately.'

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The trainer said, 'Always double-check your calculations before submitting.'
options: The trainer told us to always double-check our calculations before submitting.

quests.sentence: The trainer said, 'Always double-check your calculations before submitting.'
quests.hint: Imperative with adverb: 'told + us + to + always double-check'. 'Your' → 'our'.
quests.explanation: 'Always double-check' is an imperative → 'told us to always double-check'. 'Your calculations' shifts to 'our calculations'.
